title: We seldom can do the work we can in this world
summary: On sitting down to study or build a life, the mind floods with storm—self-blame, identity, shifting sand—and what it might mean to stand instead on the stable ground of a defined goal.

tiles.label: We seldom can do the work we can in this world

blocks.text: We seldom can do the work we can in this world.

A person, a student, sits with a decision, that he has made to study. He has lined up his goals, ambitions, desires, everything together before he opens his book and starts to read. He is motivated, he is planned, but the moment he sits on his table to work, he is deluded by the problems, anxieties, decisions, that he is facing in his life. The relationships and fights he is facing on the other ends of his life, suddenly open up and come to him the moment he starts to work. Slowly, even before he notices and realizes, his motivation is gone, he feels weak, un-energetic, lethargic, and he would take a walk, find a distraction somewhere else, like open a device, or call someone and share to feel lighter.

His breathes a bit faster, he thinks and reaches to imaginary outcomes faster, he processes things faster. Slowly as if a machine taking intense load, he feels heat inside him. Fury, anger, jealousy, ego draped as self-worth, all delude and elude him. It hurts, it pains, it crucifies, this is all that he feels. Most cry and let it out, so temporarily or for a few hours or days, they feel better, until there is a next breakout.

Some, some people elude themselves by looking inwards? What mistakes must have I made? What errors must have I  committed? They try to find spots to blame themselves, find themselves at wrong, which doesn’t really change the situation, but they just blame themselves to understand what they could have done differently.

The question is not whether the people who chose the latter option are doing it  right or wrong, they might feel that by looking at their mistakes they are at least taking responsibility and improving, but that seldom happens. Taking responsibility  is a big process, a thing a human has to actively work towards, so that he can achieve what he wants to. It can’t be only done during crash out, breakout sessions, but it happens when the river  of thoughts isn’t causing floods. It happens when it is rather still and calm, slowly following its path. That’s when the river bed is seen, that’s when clarity is observed, and thats when the rocks or obstacles in the river can be picked up and thrown at a distance.

Nevertheless, the person who performed the second task, is now so drained in the cycle of self blame and hatred that he is fully eluded from his goal and all he can do now is probably sleep or divert his mind so he feels better. Hatred, self blame drape themselves oftentimes under an impression of self-growth. Here, the student thought, he is performing a great task by looking inwards, but he is just blinded by hate and self blame that only decreases his self worth.
But…. what should a person even do then?  The emotional mental baggage is so heavy and tight, that he is just incapable of handling it all. How can he get back to his goal?
For that we need to realize one thing. So let’s answer this question.
Would you build a house on a shifting sand, or on a stable land, firm, something that feels unshakable?

The answer lies in the latter. Similarly, the latter is what is a person’s goal. A goal he has defined for himself. Now that could be what he wants to achieve in life, it could be what he wants to devote his life to, could be love, could be sports, it could be anything. But the goal is singular, non dual, its defined, its immovable, its stable.

And what are the thoughts that enter the mind, the thoughts of guilt, hate, anger, fear? This is the shifting sand. A person is not such a shifting sand that  keeps changing shapes and dimensions uncontrollably. A person keeps getting attached to such playgrounds of sand, and immerses himself in it so tightly that he starts feeling those thoughts with super intensity, and he becomes one with it. He starts identifying himself as a scared individual, a depressed individual and an anxious individual. And you would notice this person often stating to people around him  how a situation completely eroded and changed his identity. He starts blaming those situations and holding those situations, involuntarily, to explain why he is a certain way.

For example, someone dumped them and cheated on them. He becomes so attached to the negativity of that incident, that he makes it a part of his identity, and then he starts feeling scared of emotional proximity, relationships and starts doubting anyone that he comes across to. And when someone asks him why he is like that, he explains how a past incident is what he is a product of now.
Okay, but then what should that person do?

the person needs to understand he is not the shifting sand that keeps changing its forms. He is the goal that he has defined. Like a developer, he is building a house, and the thoughts that trouble  him are the stormy rains, intense heat, gusty winds, and earthquakes.

Those elements can’t be controlled, can’t be stopped by the developer. He can only pause, and redirect himself until the storm stops. On the contrary, if the developer starts feeling that the storm is what stops him from working, then the house he has to complete would either take super long to complete, or it won’t be perfectly built, or he would just give up midway. Regardless, he would assign building houses with a negative connotation in his mind.

What we need to understand is— we are the developer with a concrete goal. Winds, rains, and heat will try to stop us, and if we attach ourselves to those obstacles we would be fully derailed from our paths.
This could’ve been explained in one line, why was there such a need to write something this big?

Well, detaching ourselves from the obstacles physically is easy. Mentally its challenging. There needs to be a process, a realization, a mindset that has to be made, so that when an obstacle arrives, we are not attached to it.
What is it then? How do we detach ourselves from thoughts?

We detach ourselves from thoughts by simply noticing them. Thoughts come and go like how seasons and weather do. What stays is the goal and the self. If we decide to get carrried away with these storms, we never find a singular workable path to grow. Events, people, situations, circumstances come and go, they exit and enter our domain( the mind). We need to understand we are nothing but just a soul, who experiences these things through a window, the body, the mind, the brain, the senes, the organs, the nervous systems, but that we aren’t any of these. And it is such power of this observance that keeps us working towards what we want to achieve and separates us from the outcomes, problems, and the worldly drama.
We need to give this body a purpose, a goal, a clear path that doesn’t work on a shifting sand, but is grounded unshakably.
How does one achieve this?

This state is practiced, more than understood. Just understanding it won’t separate the self from the thoughts. It has to be practiced. How? through meditation, through explanations, and repeating to the self, “Im just a soul, only a soul. I  am not the situation, not the thought, not the vices, not the anxiety, not the worry, I  am just a soul, a soul.”
Meditation is yet another topic to be discussed further.
